sections.title: Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM) Completion
paragraphs: Code generation in IDEs rarely happens strictly from top to bottom. Codestral takes both prefix code (before cursor) and suffix code (after cursor), generating the exact bridge snippet needed.

code.label: Codestral FIM Completion Request
code.code:
from mistralai import Mistral

client = Mistral(api_key="your-api-key")
response = client.fim.complete(
    model="codestral-latest",
    prompt="def calculate_discount(price: float, discount_pct: float) -> float:\n",
    suffix="\n    return round(final_price, 2)"
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)

questions.prompt: In Codestral FIM, what does the `suffix` parameter represent?
choices: The existing source code located immediately after the editor cursor position.
The programming language compiler version number.
A financial discount code for API credits.
questions.explanation: The `suffix` parameter contains the code that follows the cursor, allowing the model to bridge the gap seamlessly without repeating subsequent lines.
